title: Signature Math Mapping — IPv4 Address Form
description: How the Signature bitstring reads as IPv4 Address Form (Numeric formats). An IPv4 address is 32 bits written as four decimal octets (e.g. 192.168.1.1). Here it is used purely as an address-FORM demonstration for 32 Signature bits.

fields.name: IPv4 Address Form
fields.system: An IPv4 address is 32 bits written as four decimal octets (e.g. 192.168.1.1). Here it is used purely as an address-FORM demonstration for 32 Signature bits.
fields.mapping: Pack the first 32 bits of the Signature string into four 8-bit octets and write them dotted-decimal. This demonstrates the address form; it does not claim the Signature is a routable network address.
apply: 1. Take the first 32 bits of the Signature string.
3. Convert each octet to decimal 0-255, join with dots.
4. Label the result 'address form — demonstration only'.
